description: Somos Bridges Mavors, un equipo de San Rafael, Mendoza, apasionado por la exploración espacial. Buscamos desarrollar un mapa interactivo de supervivencia para futuras misiones en Marte. Aportamos experiencia en desarrollo de software, diseño UX/UI y modelado 3D en Fusion 360. Si sabés de análisis de datos, mapas/SIG, narrativa o presentación de proyectos, ¡sumate a nuestro equipo! Trabajá con nosotros en un desafío real de la NASA y dejá tu huella en la exploración espacial.
summary:
Bridges Mavors is a project developed in Mendoza, Argentina, that aims to transform the exploration of Mars through MARS OPS, an interactive web platform for scientific analysis and expedition planning.

Our application combines NASA orbital maps, a 3D voxel-based representation of the Martian terrain, hazard indicators, intelligent route-planning tools, and AI-powered assistance systems.

We address this challenge by allowing users to explore the surface of Mars, access scientific information about different locations, and plan routes while taking into account terrain features, environmental conditions, and the specific needs of each expedition.

Our approach stands out for integrating these tools into a single interactive environment, prioritizing accessibility, scientific transparency, and evidence-based decision-making.

Furthermore, we seek to connect space exploration with Mendoza by proposing La Payunia as a potential terrestrial testing ground due to its geological similarities to Mars.

We believe that Bridges Mavors can help bring planetary science to a wider audience and lay the groundwork for new tools for exploration, research, and planning—both on Mars and in extreme environments on our own planet.
details:
Project Development and Functionality Bridges Mavors developed MARS OPS, an interactive web platform that integrates exploration, scientific analysis, and expedition planning tools for Mars. Our main objective is to transform large amounts of planetary data into accessible and useful resources that support informed decision-making. The application is organized as a mission control center that brings together several functionalities: - Mission Overview: Provides a summary of mission status, operational indicators, and simulated telemetry charts. - Mars Explorer: Allows users to explore NASA orbital maps and navigate a voxel-based three-dimensional representation of the Martian terrain. - Terrain Analysis: Enables users to analyze topographic characteristics and access available scientific information about specific locations. - Route Planner: Uses the A* pathfinding algorithm to calculate routes based on distance, slopes, mobility constraints, and available environmental risk data. - Scientific Targets: Organizes scientific points of interest for expeditions. - AI Systems: Incorporates a scientific assistant, image analysis tools, and resources for exploring Martian geological formations. - Aeolian Dynamics: Focuses on studying wind-driven surface processes and analyzing dune migration through observations collected at different times. - Mission Tasks: Allows users to organize expedition activities through a Kanban task management board. One of our main features is the interactive 3D map. Users can navigate the terrain, identify potentially hazardous regions, select points of interest, and plan routes directly across the surface. By right-clicking on a location, users can access scientific information associated with that specific point, depending on data availability. Benefits and Expected Impact Our platform aims to simplify access to scientific information that is typically distributed across different organizations, databases, and specialized tools. By bringing these resources together in a single environment, we seek to improve understanding of the Martian terrain, facilitate route evaluation, and support more informed expedition planning. We believe our project has significant potential for scientific research, education, and public engagement. In the long term, it could evolve into a decision-support tool for future exploration missions, provided that its models and results undergo appropriate scientific validation. We also aim to create a local impact in Mendoza, Argentina. Our province is home to extreme environments such as La Payunia, whose geological characteristics have been scientifically compared to those of Mars. We propose using this region as a potential terrestrial testing environment to evaluate and validate our navigation methodology. Tools and Technologies Used We used a combination of programming, three-dimensional visualization, scientific data processing, and artificial intelligence technologies to develop our project: - JavaScript and JSX: Application interface and interactive functionality. - React: Development of interactive user interface components. - Vite: Development environment and production build system. - HTML and CSS: Interface structure, design, and visual presentation. - Python and FastAPI: Scientific data processing and backend services. - Three.js: Three-dimensional terrain visualization and navigation. - OpenLayers: Interactive orbital map visualization. - Chart.js: Data visualization, metrics, and charts. - Blender: Three-dimensional terrain processing, adaptation, and optimization. - GeoTIFF, JSON, and GLB: Scientific, geospatial, and three-dimensional data storage and exchange. - Git and GitHub: Version control and collaboration between team members. - Codex and OpenCode: AI-assisted development and code debugging. We also worked with scientific resources from NASA Mars Trek, the Planetary Data System, Mars Global Surveyor, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, USGS, ESA, and other international research institutions. Creativity and Innovation Our proposal goes beyond simply displaying a map of Mars. We aim to transform that map into an interactive environment for scientific analysis and decision-making. We combine a voxel-based three-dimensional terrain representation with hazard indicators, location-specific scientific information, intelligent route planning, and artificial intelligence tools within a unified mission control platform. This integration allows users not only to observe the Martian surface but also to interact with it, investigate its characteristics, and understand the factors that may influence an expedition. Another distinctive aspect of our project is its connection with Mendoza. We seek to build a bridge between interplanetary exploration and the scientific and geographical capabilities of our province, demonstrating that technologies developed to explore other planets may also have valuable applications on Earth. Factors Considered During Development Throughout development, we considered the reliability of scientific sources, coordinate accuracy, differences in spatial resolution between datasets, terrain characteristics, and the limitations of available information. We also considered accessibility, usability, graphics performance, three-dimensional asset optimization, and integration between the application's different systems. Scientific transparency was one of our main priorities. We distinguish observed data, derived results, modeled conditions, and simulations, avoiding presenting unknown information as established scientific fact. For example, we differentiate observed dune migration measurements from future predictions, which require further model training and validation. Through Bridges Mavors, we aim to demonstrate how science, programming, creativity, and teamwork can contribute to new ways of exploring Mars, making space science more accessible and creating opportunities for innovation from Mendoza to the world.
